forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Current price of 330 USc/lb is well-supported by persistent weather stress across producer belts; a plunge below 300 in two months is improbable.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: At 330 USc/lb, prices would need an unusually abrupt collapse over two months to breach 300 USc/lb, which supply adjustments do not warrant so quickly.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Spot prices sit at 330 USc/lb. Short-term harvesting noise in Vietnam won't undo structural global tightening fast enough to break 300 USc/lb by December.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: While coffee is softening, plunging 30 cents in two months overstates short-term velocity. Prices generally digest gains slowly, staying above 300.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Coffee sits well above 300 USc/lb with broad commodity strength providing a cushion; short-term collapse in two months is improbable.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Despite recent softening, global coffee inventories are not fully replenished, keeping prices comfortably above 300 USc/lb through year-end.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Global supply chains remain sensitive to extreme weather, keeping wholesale prices above 300 cents despite short-term market adjustments.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Prices remain elevated around 330 USc/lb; with compounding climate extremes in producer regions, a steep drop below 300 by December is unlikely.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Strong El Niño conditions and general freight cost pressures should keep mild coffee above the 300 USc/lb floor into December.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Despite incoming harvest supplies, tight global pipeline inventories and high baseline prices make defending the 300 USc/lb support likely over the next sixty days.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Despite recent farmgate price easing, spot market inertia and shipping frictions should keep EU wholesale coffee prices above 300 USc/lb through year-end.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Despite recent wholesale easing, strong baseline import parity and pipeline logistics keep spot levels above 300 USc/lb through year-end.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Current price of 330 USc/lb provides some buffer, though downside pressure is accelerating. The market price fairly reflects two-month decay.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Spot market is softening quickly toward 300 USc/lb as supply returns, though shipping lane friction slows total capitulation.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: The crowd prices this at 53%. Spot prices dropped toward 330 USc/lb with recent bearish harvest reports, nudging us slightly down.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Supply normalization is gathering speed, pulling prices downward as roasters face weaker demand and expanding supply.
